decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and blind target 0 identify Duke and Bègue (2015) (DOI: 10.1016/j.cognition.2014.09.006) as the tested original study. Primary evidence confirms that this preregistered experiment directly re-tests Duke and Bègue's (2015) 'drunk utilitarian' finding on the footbridge and switch trolley dilemmas (as well as CNI model and OUS extensions).

decisions.quote:
This preregistered experiment aimed to provide deeper insights into the effects of alcohol on moral judgments by
                                 using a formal modeling approach to disentangle three factors in moral dilemma judgments and by distinguishing between
                                 instrumental harm and impartial beneficence as two distinct dimensions of utilitarian psychology. Despite the use of a
                                 substantially larger sample and higher doses of alcohol compared with the ones in prior studies, alcohol had no significant
                                 effect on moral judgments. The results pose a challenge to the idea that alcohol increases utilitarianism in moral judgments.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding classify the record as 'replication'. The paper collects new experimental data from 329 participants randomly assigned to alcohol, placebo, and no-alcohol conditions to re-test the previously published 'drunk utilitarian' finding.
